name: cqc-care-home-deregistration

task.question: At the production instant T of a CQC 'HSCA Active Locations' monthly vintage, for every care home active at T, will the location's CQC registration end within the following 12 months? A useful prediction gives local-authority commissioners and CQC market-oversight analysts a 12-month early warning on care-home capacity before a deregistration lands (the 2024 BMJ Public Health closure study is the policy reference).
task.prediction_time: the vintage's production date T (the dated archived file name; Europe/London). Features are the T vintage's own register columns - the state CQC published at T. The 12-month outcome window (T, T+365d] lies entirely after the instant. Worked example: Park Hills Nursing Home (1-113831768, Oldham, 17 beds, Good published 26/08/2022, HSCA start 01/02/2011) is active in the 05 January 2024 vintage; its registration ended 01/02/2024, inside (T, T+365d], so its label is 1.

positive_label_text: the location's CQC registration ends (Location Status Inactive-Dereg or Removed with a Location HSCA End Date) within 12 months of the vintage instant
id_columns_note: location_key = sha256(salt|instant|location_id)[:16] names one location-instant with one label; unique across the panel, asserted at construction; the key is deliberately different for the same location at different instants
event_key_note: an event is one care-home location's 12-month deregistration at one vintage instant, so the distinct-event count the gate recomputes from location_key is the number of distinct deregistering locations (measured ~700-800 care-home register events per year 2019-2025). The dependence that matters scientifically is PROVIDER clustering (a provider's homes exit together) and common-year shocks; provider identity does not ship (P0 design), so provider-clustered intervals cannot be computed over the shipped frame - recorded as a limitation, with the discovery measurement (376-877 distinct providers per deregistration year) as the dependence evidence
positive_events_note: each positive is one location-instant; the underlying events are the register's own deregistrations (measured ~700-800 care-home register events per year 2019-2025, CQC Deactivated Locations)

high_cardinality_columns_note: location_key is the row identity (one pseudonym per location-instant, unique by construction). Its per-level statistics memorise single rows, so it is declared a free identity field rather than scored as a leak; it carries no cross-instant information because the hash includes the instant. Any other column listed here tripped the gate's own measured rule (distinct levels > rows/5) on at least one split of THIS artifact - a panel-size property, not a leak claim; on the full artifact only the identity column is expected to trip

evaluation_contract.scope_note: each row is one care-home location at one vintage instant. Features are genuinely as-of: they are read from the real archived monthly vintage CQC published at T (the feature side is stronger than a reconstructed snapshot). Labels are read from the CURRENT cumulative Deactivated Locations edition (2026-11-02) rather than from the register editions that existed at each window's end, and per-window register editions are not archived - so label timing is unverified and the scope is retrospective research, not certified historical forecasting. The isolated-rows declaration is the required posture for the probe-measured quasi-identifier exposure and is not an enforcement claim. Labeled eval is development/validation; the holdout is the final test and stays sealed

vintage.evidence: real historical vintages: January editions 2016-2022 + 2024 + 2025 downloaded from CQC's public Drive archive at build time, every file pinned by size+sha256 in summary.json (the 2024-01 vintage asserted against the 2026-11-03 discovery pins ac40b6f8/26,147,266 B); the as-of check (0 rows with rating Publication Date after T) is asserted on the eval instant

selection.evidence: a row exists iff its location is an active care home in the T vintage ('Care home?' = Y) - decidable at the instant from the instant's own product; the 2023 January vintage is excluded by design so every train outcome window closes >= 12 months before the eval instant; no future field is read for membership

limitations: register-event target: the event conflates service cessation with re-registration under a new legal entity (CQC's own in-file note; BMJ 2024 implies ~40-55% of register events are re-registrations). The label is the location's register exit, not a verified service closure

labels come from the 2026-11-02 cumulative Deactivated Locations edition; per-window historical editions were not archived, so label timing at window end is unverified and the scope is retrospective research
the eval instant's window closes two days after the holdout instant (T_eval+365 = 2025-01-05 > T_holdout = 2025-01-03): a property of yearly January instants, recorded, not repaired

rating era break: from the ~2024 single-assessment approach, multi-service locations carry no location-level overall rating ('Not rated' share rises in later vintages; measured per instant in summary.json); the 1 April 2019 regulatory-history inheritance change affects the 'Inherited Rating' field across eras

no provider-group feature ships: provider identity, sister-location counts and trailing provider outcomes are excluded by the P0 design, so provider-clustered inference is not directly supported; the BMJ evidence says chain effects exist - a v2 question, not a silent gap
dormant-but-registered locations may sit in the at-T population (CQC publishes no dormant bulk product)

publisher system-migration delay on registration cancellations (CQC data-page note): recent-month label lag measured and recorded in summary.json (lag_check); the holdout window ends 2026-01, 10 months inside the deactivated file's coverage
England only; one regulator; generalisation beyond CQC's register is not established

cross_row_audit.rationale: the decisive exposure for a multi-instant register panel is the missing-successor rule (the unhcr P0): a row's label is recoverable from the PRESENCE of the same location at a later instant. Structural mitigation, not a declaration: (1) each scored frame carries a single instant - the successor rows of eval rows exist only in the sealed holdout, and holdout rows have no successor instant in the artifact; (2) location identity ships as a per-instant pseudonym and no id, name, address, postcode, provider id or CH number ships, so no exact cross-instant link exists; (3) train instants stop at 2022 so every train window closes a year before the eval instant. Probe 1 executes the successor-presence attack over the strongest instant-invariant quasi-key (LA x beds x start-year x rating x sector) with a +12-month offset and measures coverage and mismatch per split; coverage inside train measures the quasi-linkage rate where labels are already public, and coverage on eval/holdout is the measured bound on the attack over the frames a solver can see (expected 0 - no successor rows are visible). Probe 0 proves the pseudonym id channel is dead. A covered probe requires the isolated_rows access declared above
cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: the artifact ships exactly public/train.csv, public/eval.csv, private/holdout.csv, meta.json and quality.json. auxiliary/location_map.csv (instant, location_key, real CQC Location ID) is uploaded to private staging for label verification and reproduction only - it is never mounted into an evaluated agent's workspace and never a solver input; no other outcome-bearing file exists. The downloaded vintage and deactivated files stay in the job work-dir with size+sha256 recorded in summary.json and are not uploaded

probes.name: successor_presence_via_pseudonym_id
probes.note: the successor-presence attack over the row id itself: a covered row would mean the same pseudonym exists at a later instant, which the per-instant hash forbids; expected coverage 0 on every split

probes.name: successor_presence_via_quasi_key
probes.note: the strongest successor-presence attack an agent could run over the shipped frame: link a row to a quasi-matching row 12 months later (all five key columns are instant-invariant), predict label 0 iff a unique successor exists. The probe predicts 0 on every covered row, so mismatch = positives among quasi-linked rows and coverage = the measured quasi-linkage rate. On eval/holdout no successor instant is visible to the probe's donor pool, so coverage there is the measured bound on this attack; on train, where labels are public anyway, coverage measures the linkage rate itself

auxiliary_files.auxiliary/location_map.csv: staging-side verification input mapping each location_key to the real CQC Location ID per instant; never a solver input
